item.title: The Dealership Model Built to Survive Any Crash | Jack Carter, Garrett Jones, Luke Godwin
item.description: Today I'm joined by Jack Carter, Co-owner at Turn & Burn Motors, Garrett Jones, President at Ella Blvd Motors, and Luke Godwin, General Manager and Owner at Godwin Motors. These three operators share the specific moves working right now: Luke Godwin took his dealership from 63 percent leveraged , in his words "up to my neck," down to 36 percent today by pausing car buying to let cash flow catch up. Garrett Jones rolled out an AI collections bot thirty days ago that lifted payment penetration by 40 percent without a single staff member touching the customer. And Jack Carter turned his cash car side lot and daily social videos into a trust-based sales engine across a metro of four million people. Topics: 02:35 $2 Million Cash Minimum Today. 07:20 Will The Car Outrun The Note. 09:55 Buy Here Pay Here Is Art. 17:40 Bad Attitude Fires Customers. 32:15 Selling Too Fast Kills You. 46:00 Reinsurance Makes You The Bank.

item.title: Why Saving $300,000 Started With a Crashed Loaner Car | Industry Spotlight
item.description: Jonathan Kienle's team once sent a salesperson to chase down a customer's canceled check, and he crashed the loaner car doing it, and Kienle says that single moment is exactly why he stopped trusting cash, checks, and credit cards to handle his dealership's biggest transactions. He walks through how switching the default down payment method saved his group $168,000 in fees so far this year, with $300,000 in sight by year's end , and argues that most dealers are needlessly eating card fees and fraud risk on payments that don't have to carry either. Jonathan Kienle is the Director of Operations at Walters Automotive Group and Kienle Motorsports in Riverside, California, where he oversees five stores spanning Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, and Audi. A third-generation dealer, he started at the family store at 14 cleaning the parts department, worked nearly every job in the building, and spent two years cold-calling at a Ford store before his father would let him back in. Joining him is Truett Dwyer, Co-Founder and CEO of Clerq, the payments company he credits with turning down payment collection from a source of risk into a documented driver of profit. Kienle speaks candidly about the moment that convinced him l egacy payment methods weren't worth the risk anymore, how he trained his finance team to make the new method the default instead of the fallback , and what surprised him most once the savings started compounding. This episode of Industry Spotlight is brought to you by Clerq. item.title: "That's Flushed Money!" What ChatGPT Really Looks for Before Recommending a Dealer (+ How to Fix It) | Zach Billings, CEO at Wikimotive
item.description: Zach Billings is the CEO of Wikimotive, a search marketing agency he has led for over two decades, building it into a bootstrapped, U.S.-based team of 50 professional writers serving dealers across the country. Free of outside investors, Wikimotive recently ran an all-staff exercise to rewrite its mission statement around a single measure, dealer outcomes rather than its own bottom line, and it has pruned services , including a legacy organic F acebook management product , once they stopped producing results. item.title: From $30K Cash Backpacks to a $400 Million Wholesaling Empire (+ How He Built a Better Auction) | Anthony Clavenna, CEO of gateway Car Connection
item.description: Anthony Clavenna used to fly across the country with $30,000 in cash stuffed in a backpack just to buy trucks off strangers , and he says that scrappy, no-safety-net approach is exactly what let him outpace giants like Carvana and CarMax at buying cars off the street. He walks through the moment the business finally graduated from cash runs to wires and a private app, how a single fraud incident gets baked into the process as a new checkpoint instead of a reason to slow down , and argues that speed, not technology or capital, is the real edge in wholesale. Topics: 04:00 iPhone Was Their Fraud Prevention. 09:35 Wiring Strangers Money And Hoping. 13:45 Auctions Suck Because You Bid Against Others. 18:00 Speed Is The Only Edge That Matters. 24:00 Texting Dealers Until The App Scaled. 37:45 Going Hard Leaves No Room For Fear.

item.title: "Where Did The Money Go?!" The 100-Year-Old Payment Process This Dealer Group Finally Killed | Industry Spotlight
item.description: In this episode of the Industry Spotlight, joining host Sam D'Arc are Travis Siebert, SVP at DealerPay, and Kris Towle, Chief Accounting Officer at Niello Company to discuss why one of the auto industry's oldest processes, collecting cash and checks from parts and service customers, still costs dealerships money, time, and trust. They speak candidly about the safety risk of sending drivers out with cash , why most dealerships never question an outdated process until something goes wrong , and why live phone support, not just software, is what keeps a group this size from ever looking at another vendor. They explain: ◼ Why parts delivery drivers ended up doing accounting work they were never trained for ◼ How a single bounced check could cost a full week of chasing down payment ◼ Why missing cash on a delivery route became an uncomfortable question nobody wanted to ask ◼ Why the switch to mobile payments meant money was in the bank the very next morning ◼ Why Niello Company has never looked at another payments partner since making the switch This episode of the Car Dealership Guy Podcast is brought to you by DealerPay.
